article.headline: Exxon Mobil Hits All-Time High As Quarterly Earnings More Than Double
article.deck: Exxon broke out of a 27-week cup on Oct. 14 and trades 0.9% above its 176.51 buy point, inside a buy range that runs to 185.34.
body: Exxon Mobil finds and produces crude oil and natural gas in the U.S., Canada and abroad, then turns much of it into fuels, chemicals and lubricants. It reports four segments: upstream production; energy products such as fuels, aromatics and catalysts; chemical products such as olefins and polyolefins; and specialty products including finished lubricants and basestocks.

The June quarter explains the stock's climb. EPS was 3.48, up 112.2% from a year earlier, on revenue of $114.53 billion, up 44.1%. That was a sharp turn rather than a steady climb. EPS had slipped from 1.76 in the September 2025 quarter to 1.53 in December and 1.00 in March, and revenue had sat between $80.04 billion and $83.33 billion for three quarters. The next report, on Oct. 30, will show whether June was a peak or a new level.

The market values Exxon at $732.3 billion. Shares trade at 14.6 times forward earnings, against 22.9 times trailing, so the price assumes earnings stay higher than they were a year ago. The stock is up 48.0% this year and 58.0% over 12 months.

On the chart, Exxon closed up 0.23, or 0.1%, at 178.09 on Wednesday. The cup ran 27 weeks and 23.5% deep, from a March 30 high to a June 25 low. The stock cleared the 176.51 buy point on Oct. 14, when volume was 1.0x its 50-day average. Wednesday's session traded 0.84x. The close is 0.9% above the buy point and 1.2% below the 52-week high of 180.26.

Exxon is 8.0% above its 50-day line at 164.92 and 1.51 ATRs from the 21-day line at 170.70, an intact trend that is not stretched. RS rank is 82 of 99 on the desk's list, though the RS line is 15.1% below its high. Exxon also has company. Energy ranks third among the desk's groups with an average RS rank of 62, and ConocoPhillips, EOG and Chevron broke out the same week.
A Tuesday headline said Exxon Mobil hit a new all-time high. Another asked whether the company can strengthen its long-term upstream production capacity.
article.watch: The Oct. 30 report, and whether the stock holds the 176.51 buy point into it.

article.deck: Fortinet bounced off its 50-day line and closed 2.1% above its 170.45 buy point, inside a buy range that runs to 178.97.
body: Fortinet rose 3.12, or 1.8%, to 174.05 on Wednesday, rebounding from its 50-day moving average. The stock broke out Aug. 27 from a six-week cup that ran 15.6% deep from a July 15 high to a July 29 low. The buy point is 170.45, and Wednesday's close is 2.1% above it, inside the buy range that tops out at 178.97. Volume was 0.75x the 50-day average, a light session. The breakout day traded 1.26x.

Shares are 11.7% below the 52-week high of 197.13. The 50-day line sits at 170.01, 2.4% under the close, while the 21-day exponential average is at 178.31. At -0.44 ATRs from the 21-day line, the session's high stayed under that average: the stock is working back from a pullback, not running away. The breakout is 38 sessions old. RS rank is 93 of 99 on the desk's list, though the RS line is 10.0% off its high. Fortinet is up 119.2% this year and 105.1% over 12 months.

In the June quarter Fortinet earned 0.82 a share, up 43.9% from a year earlier, on revenue of $2.05 billion, up 25.6%. EPS has risen in each of the four quarters given, from 0.62 to 0.68, 0.72 and 0.82. The next report is due Oct. 28. Market value is $127.7 billion, at 45.9 times forward earnings.

The gain came despite a morning headline that the stock fell as Arete delivered a rare double downgrade to sell. On Tuesday, CBTS and Fortinet launched a fully managed secure networking service for mid-market organizations.
A close back under the 50-day line, which sits just below the buy point, would put the breakout in doubt going into earnings.
